source.version_note: Published 20 July 2026, Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research 21:234. Archival reviews cover 2016–2021; vignette experiment collected July 2024.

citation.title: Crossing the AI Mind Trap: Deconstructing the Impact of AI Mind Perception on User Engagement in AI Voice Assistants
citation.venue: Journal of Theoretical and Applied Electronic Commerce Research, 21:234

reading.source_scope_note: An observational price-tier/text-classification study and a randomized hypothetical smart-product-description experiment. Measures concern human review content and engagement intentions, not actual current LLM mental states, longitudinal engagement or observed identity-threat/overload mediators.
access_limits: All 24 extracted pages read, including all ten tables, Appendix A's five full vignettes, ethics declarations and references. Page 11 curve/UTEST and page 16 experimental plot visually inspected.
Raw reviews, trained classifier, exact engagement questionnaire, participant data and analysis code were not obtained or rerun. Cited primary studies of ambivalence and uncanny mind were not read.

study_1.source: JD reviews of Baidu DuerOS smart screens, stated 11 June 2016–14 October 2021
study_1.mind_proxy: Four product/price tiers coded 1–4, analyzed on a log scale; no direct individual mind-perception measure
study_1.engagement_proxy: Sum of three 0/1 classifier labels: family-oriented cognitive relevance, positive affect and repurchase/recommendation
study_1.training_labels: 1100 reviews, two coders; reported Cronbach alpha>.7
study_1.overall_shape_test: t=1.32, p=.0926; turning point .931 on log scale, 95% Fieller interval [.742,2.698], observed log range [0,1.386]

study_2.exclusions: 2 rapid completions and 11 failed mind-level checks
study_2.design: Randomized five hypothetical descriptions: low/low, medium/medium, high/high, high-agency/low-experience, low-agency/high-experience
study_2.H1_subset: 149, overlapping low/low, medium/medium and high/high groups
study_2.H2_subset: 198, four low/high factorial corners; medium group excluded
study_2.outcome: Four self-report likelihood items on a seven-point scale, not observed usage

summary: Add attitudinal ambivalence from an explicit secondary definition. Enrich anthropomorphism with a qualified human vignette result, while excluding the claimed uncanny-valley and overload mechanisms from corroborating counts. The price-tier proxy, marginal shape test, interval error and bundled scope/communication manipulations prevent the paper from establishing a universal optimum for AI mind or engagement.

findings.definition: Coexisting positive and negative evaluations of the same target within a person.
findings.novelty_rationale: Explicitly defined secondary construct absent from the current primary entries. Different from uncertainty, a neutral average, alternating judgments, logical contradiction or the distress/reduction process of cognitive dissonance. It is a potentially reasonable evaluative state, not an inherently harmful failure.

evidence.quote: attitudes (i.e., the coexistence of positive and negative attitudes) toward mindful AI robots

findings.evidence_scope: Secondary description of Dang and Liu (2021), reference 44, studying mindful/mindless robots in the United States and China. That primary is unread. This paper does not separately measure simultaneous positive and negative evaluations or a validated ambivalence index.
findings.boundary: A medium group scoring above a high group is not within-person ambivalence. Neither a midpoint nor a mixture of different people's positive and negative ratings proves coexistence in one person. Balanced recognition of benefits and costs can be warranted. An AI giving both favorable and unfavorable assessments does not establish felt conflict or human affect.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human attitude construct defined secondarily; ambivalence itself not measured in the present studies
findings.ai_proposal: Measure positive and negative evaluations separately for the same target and person, distinguishing simultaneous ambivalence from uncertainty and between-person disagreement. For AI output, assess whether both evaluations are grounded and whether the decision explains their tradeoff; do not force false certainty or infer subjective feelings.

findings.term: Human-trait descriptions can change engagement intentions without proving machine feelings
findings.definition: Descriptions of agency and experience can alter people's intended engagement, but their effects depend on the other task, communication and authorization features included in those descriptions.
findings.novelty_rationale: Adds a direct human description experiment with explicit manipulation-content limits rather than a new anthropomorphism synonym or a measured internal model state.

evidence.quote: asked to read instructions describing Smart Product X in detail
execute actions that you may not have intended

findings.evidence_scope: 249 retained participants assigned to five vignettes. Reported intended engagement is highest for medium overall mind (5.823), followed by agentic (5.577), high (5.092), experiential (4.775) and mindless (3.791). The published omnibus tests do not individually establish every pairwise contrast or the proposed mediator.
findings.boundary: The low condition cannot communicate in natural language, the medium condition stays within the assigned task, and high-agency conditions may execute unintended actions. The experiment therefore changes practical capability and scope as well as attributed mind. Claimed hunger, pain and feelings are vignette assertions, not evidence of actual AI experience or a recommendation to make such claims.

findings.term: An inverted-U intention pattern is not full uncanny-valley evidence
findings.definition: A fitted concave relationship or a preference for a medium description does not alone establish a local eeriness dip near human likeness with subsequent recovery.
findings.novelty_rationale: Clarifies the difference between the authors' broad uncanny-mind interpretation and the narrower existing concept boundary.

evidence.quote: followed by participants in the high mindful Smart Product X group

findings.evidence_scope: Study 1's overall UTEST is marginal at .1, not significant at .05; its turning-point interval exceeds the observed log-tier range. Study 2 has three overall-mind descriptions with confounded features and no direct eeriness/affinity measure or recovery condition.
findings.boundary: Keep the paper as a qualified related reference rather than a corroborating demonstration of the full valley. Lower intention can reflect justified concerns about unintended action, communication differences or stated needs, not aversion caused by a uniquely humanlike mind.

findings.term: Information and emotional overload are proposed, not measured mediators
findings.definition: The authors interpret lower engagement under some experiential descriptions through information/emotion overload, while explicitly acknowledging that no such mediator was measured.
findings.novelty_rationale: Records a future explanatory lead without filling a cognitive-load evidence gap or treating an unmeasured pathway as established.

evidence.quote: these psychological variables were not formally modeled or measured as

findings.evidence_scope: Theory-level interpretation in the discussion; no workload, information volume, emotional burden or reasoning-degradation measure.
findings.boundary: Lower willingness to engage is not evidence that cognitive capacity was exceeded. Measure the proposed burden separately and compare alternative explanations such as task relevance, consent, practical usefulness and misleading claims of need.

methodological_limits: Study 1 operationalizes mind perception as price/model tier, not individual attribution. Hardware, audience, release date, use case, affordability and expectations can confound that proxy. Rating/software controls do not validate the construct or neutralize all hardware effects.

The response proxy sums family-oriented relevance, positive sentiment and repurchase/recommendation mentions. It is not an observed longitudinal usage measure and may miss deep negative engagement or cognition unrelated to family. Customer reviews remain self-reports despite being archival.

20,779 review rows share a small set of models and four tier values. No clustered product/user/time error treatment is reported in the supplied model; row count is not the number of independently varied machine minds.

Coding reliability is described using Cronbach alpha rather than a clearly specified interrater-agreement statistic. Class balance, per-label confusion matrices, calibration and exact nested validation are not provided. Classifier performance does not establish validity of the psychological proxy, and prediction uncertainty is not propagated into regression.

Product tiers are ordinal, and taking their numeric/log distances assumes a particular spacing. Only four values constrain the fitted curvature. The quadratic adds only .0002 to R-squared over the linear tier model (.1514 to .1516).

Table 6 reports overall inverted-U p=.0926 and upper-slope t=-1.325. This is marginal under a .1 criterion, not conventional .05 evidence. The P>|t| labeling should be reconciled with the apparent one-sided value rather than silently interpreted as a standard two-sided p.
The text says the 95% turning-point interval lies within the observed range, but [.742,2.698] exceeds [0,1.386] on the log scale. The estimated peak .931 is within range; its entire interval is not.

Figure 1 labels x as mind perception but plots its apparent log scale and negative y values despite a 0–3 outcome. The curve closely follows the intercept plus mind terms, rather than the full prediction using Table 5 control means. Its caption claims controls at their means; exact plotting code is needed to reconcile this.

Logit/probit curvature on recoded versions of the same classifier labels does not independently validate mind perception or the full shape test. Winsorizing a four-level variable may change little; subgroup counts and detailed robustness results are not supplied.

Study 1's 2016–2021 smart-screen reviews and Study 2's July 2024 hypothetical descriptions do not directly evaluate current LLM-enabled assistants. Device launch dates, model availability, version assignments and the early review window need raw-record verification before interpreting technology trends.

Study 2 excludes 11 people based on a mind-level comprehension/manipulation question after exposure. Allocation-specific exclusions and sensitivity to retaining them are not reported; random assignment of scenarios does not make the recruited online sample representative.

Appendix A contradicts the claim that natural-language communication is held constant: the mindless product cannot communicate in natural language, while other conditions can. Medium mind is task-bounded; high-agency descriptions may act beyond user intentions. Experience conditions add expressed feelings and needs. These bundles do not isolate one amount of mind.

Perceived agency is not identical to competence, and experience is not identical to warmth. An agent can be socially warm without felt experience; the article's conceptual mapping should not erase these distinctions.

Engagement is intended engagement after reading a vignette, not actual ongoing interaction, retention or investment. Higher experience conditions remain above the mindless mean, so lower relative intention does not establish absolute aversion or eeriness.

Omnibus ANCOVA significance does not itself test the specific medium-versus-high contrast or the agency-by-experience interaction. The four corner cells permit a 2x2 interaction analysis, but the reported one-way omnibus alone is insufficient for that mechanistic claim.

The reported F(2,146) and F(3,194) alongside covariate descriptions have group-effect degrees of freedom, not three-covariate degrees of freedom. The separate adjusted omnibus tests use denominator 143/191. Clarify which tests concern covariates rather than infer from the prose.

Presence is measured after the scenario and used as a covariate. If influenced by treatment, adjustment can remove part of the effect or introduce bias; it should not be assumed equivalent to a pre-treatment control.

The two experiment subsets overlap in low/high groups, so they are not independent replications. The study does not measure within-person positive/negative ambivalence, identity threat, perceived loss of control or overload as causal mediators.

Section 3.2.1 says the university ethics committee formally reviewed and approved the experiment, whereas the final IRB statement says approval was not required. These inconsistent declarations need author clarification; neither establishes a conclusion of unlawful research by this review.

Public accessibility of reviews does not by itself prove no privacy implications. The article says avatars were collected and terms/robots compliance followed; those claims were not independently audited, and no legal determination is made here.

The opening market figure cites a US smart-home market report. That broader category is not automatically a voice-assistant-only market; scope needs verification before reuse. Managerial recommendations to grant authority or express feelings do not follow as tested safety or truthfulness outcomes.
No raw dataset, model code or exact engagement item set was independently obtained. Reliability alphas and external cited studies do not replace such checks.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Identity-description and mind-description manipulations both affect human evaluations, but the present vignettes bundle authorization, communication and emotional-expression features. Do not treat them as clean replications of the negotiation identity effect.
Apparent emotion or social capacity is not actual subjective experience. Human reactions to described or mocked agents must remain distinct from observed model behaviour and verified internal agency.

deferred.reason: Related manifestation of the existing uncanny-valley concept, with incomplete shape and construct evidence. Do not add a duplicate or promote the authors' broad interpretation to a proven independent mechanism.

Secondary proposed explanation about compromised uniqueness/control, not directly measured or sufficiently separated from existing self-humanization and social-comparison coverage here. Read its primary study before a standalone entry.
Explicitly unmeasured proposed pathway. Existing cognitive-load boundary note records it without adding duplicate overload mechanisms.
Broad agency/experience framework rather than a newly isolated behaviour; retain distinctions through existing mentalizing/anthropomorphism/sociomorphism links.

limitations: One secondary human attitude construct added; it is not claimed to be measured in this paper or experienced by AI.
No universal engagement optimum, full uncanny-valley replication, tested overload pathway or current LLM mentality inferred from the proxies and vignettes.
